TAN Secretary to the Sanggunian Office of the Secretary to the Sanggunian Municipality of Don Marcelino Province of Davao Occidental Dear Mr. Tan: This refers to your letter addressed to Abdullah V. Matalam, DILG XI Regional Director, requesting for this Department's opinion on the inconsistency between the DILG Memorandum Circular 2024-1091 and Municipal Ordinance No. 18 Section 14 and 15 series of 2023.2 We respond. Under Section 447(a)(3)(v) of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Govemment Code of 1991, the sangguniang bayan is empowered to authorize and license the establishment, operation, and maintenance of cockpits, and to regulate cockfighting and commercial breeding of gamecocks. Relatedly, Sections 5(d) and 5(e) of Presidential Decree No. 449, or the Cockfighting Law of 1974, provide that special cockfights may be held on the occasion of local festivities or other approved events, subject to the approval of the local Chief of Police and the favorable resolution of the concerned sanggunian. In this context, DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2024-109 reiterates the requirement that no special cockfighting event may be authorized absent such resolution and approval, which remains consistent with the above-cited provisions of the Local Government Code and PD 449. Notably, the Supreme Court in Tan v. Penera3,has affirmed that the Local Government Code must still be read in harmony with limitations under PD 4494, particularly in matters involving cockfighting regulation. Reminders on the Operation of Cockpits and the conduct of Cockfighting Activities 2 The Municipal Mayor is authorizæd to issue special permit for the conduct of cockfighting during the Araw ng Barangay for one-day period Only upon resolution Of the Sangguniang Barangay Concerned and in Section 15, the Sangguniang Bayan through a Resolution may issue a Special Permit for the conduct or cockfighting for agricultural, commercial or industrial fair, carnival or exposition and likewise the entertainment of foreign dignitaries, tourists, or Filipino Balikbayans or for the support of national tUnd-raising campaign for a period of not more than three (3) days. GR No. 149743 February 18, 2005 (d) Holding Of Cockfights — Except as provided in this Decree, cockfighting shall be allowed only in licensed cockpits during Sunday and legal Holidays and during local fiestas for not more than three days. It may also be held during provincial, city or municipal, agricultural, commercial or industrial fair, carnival or exposition for a Similar period of three days upon resolution of the province, city or municipality where such fair, carnival or "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

As regards the enforceability of Municipal Ordinance No. 18, series of 2023, we reiterate that ordinances enjoy a presumption of validity unless declared otherwise by a court of competent jurisdiction. It is settled that for a municipal ordinance to be valid, it must: (a) not contravene the Constitution or statute; (b) not be unfair, oppressive, or discriminatory; (c) not prohibit but may regulate trade; (d) not be unreasonable; and (e) be general in application and consistent with public policy5. Finally, with respect to the potential liability of local officials in the implementation of the subject ordinance, it bears emphasis that such matter involves factual and legal determinations that are best addressed through appropriate judicial proceedings. Questions relating to administrative or criminal accountability must be resolved by the proper tribunals based on established facts and applicable laws. As such, this Department refrains from rendering any categorical position thereon. This opinion is rendered solely on the basis of the facts and representations presented and is without prejudice to any contrary ruling or opinion by competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, By the Authority of tte Secretary: ATTY. ROMEO P.
